newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary coalition party calls on minister to quit.
newsitem.headline: Hungary coalition party calls on minister to quit.

text.p: The Free Democrats, junior partner in Hungary's coalition government, called on Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman to resign over a scandal involving illegal payments by the privatisation agency which falls under his control.
"This can lead to a coalition crisis if Tamas Suchman is not fired...," Free Democrat chairman Ivan Peto told a radio interviewer.

The Hungarian government on Friday sacked the entire board of privatisation agency APV Rt, saying it had made irregular payments amounting to millions of dollars to lawyer Marta Tocsik, who negotiated with municipalities on APV's behalf.
The government spared Suchman, although opposition parties said he was responsible and should go.
Prime Minister Gyula Horn, who at a meeting of the senior coalition partner Hungarian Socialisty Party on Saturday defended his minister, plans to review the issue on Monday.

Suchman's dismissal was not immediately effective because the next person in line at the ministry has resigned following Suchman's nomination as industry and trade minister in September, Horn told Hungarian Television's "The Week" news programme.
